description: Minimum Tauri permissions the webview actually uses. The Rust host owns the Go sidecar lifecycle (spawn/kill via std::process — no shell plugin needed); the webview invokes two custom commands (get_backend_config, restart_backend) plus opens external URLs via shellOpen. Spawn/kill/execute were previously granted and represented pure gratuitous authority an XSS payload would inherit. shell:allow-open only enables the open command: tauri-plugin-shell 2.x validates what `open` may receive against tauri.conf.json > plugins > shell > open (the ACL scope for this permission covers execute/spawn entries, not URLs), and that validator is pinned to https URLs. The only caller is the device-auth verification_uri; the reveal-in-explorer adapter method that once passed bare filesystem paths was unused and has been removed (Reveal in file manager goes through the backend's /api/flow/reveal).
